learning_outcomes.text: Students know basic electrical conduction mechanisms. They can describe the propagation properties of lines important for information and energy transmission.

Students who have successfully studied this module have the necessary basic knowledge about the behavior of real passive electronic components, which is required for calculating electrical networks with time-varying voltages and currents. They are also aware of the temperature dependence of component properties and their aging behavior.

After successful completion of the module, students are able to calculate the behavior of real passive electronic components under time-varying excitation. They can make statements about the failure rate of components.

Students who have successfully completed this module recognize the influence of environmental conditions and component properties on the reliability of electrical systems. Furthermore, they can calculate the propagation delay effects for signals on lines.

Students who have successfully completed this module can exchange ideas with other students about the problems they are working on and can organize appropriate cooperation among themselves. They can suitably summarize the results of their experimental work in a short report.

syllabus_topics: Behavior of real passive components (equivalent circuits, parasitic properties, aging, reliability)
Line theory: Line equations, reflection and characteristic impedance
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam (Klausur) as per the valid study regulations. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 5 experiments, each lasting 90 minutes. ECTS credits are awarded based on these assessments.
bibliography: T. Harriehausen, D. Schwarzenau: „Moeller Grundlagen der Elektrotechnik", Springer Vieweg
